interpretation: Sample verified: two terminal fresh-rootfs read-only runs, eight fixed-input calls, and the complete prior generated-configuration pipeline preserved. Actual signed LOAD32 results and destination-slot write identities are joined to later VM scalar stores. The MD5 middle word reloads an earlier scalar store at BCP +0x9aabc, whose LOAD32 at BCP +0x9aab8 reaches the decoder prefix through a constructor copy. The SHA-1 last word also reaches that decoder prefix, and the SHA-1 first word reaches the configuration-decrypt plaintext prefix through two copies. Each source join checks snapshots, actual per-byte write-event identity and temporal order; decoder and plaintext terminal writer sets are retained as module-relative instruction locations. The three shared-word consumers use the same observed source address and equal snapshots, but no writer event covers those bytes in the instrumented per-call window. Their common address lies in a readable/writable, nonexecutable mapping outside the observed native stack and current VM register bank. This does not identify the allocation, initialization, lifetime, host/provider writer, global/TLS owner, zero value, constant or independent generation of that word. Existing Python bridge bytes match the parent checkpoint. Encoded configuration origin, reduction leaves, lookup key, other inputs, actual Android allocator/singleton equivalence, complete standalone signer and ordinary Cronet six-header online acceptance remain unverified. No operand bytes, keys/IVs, plaintext, runtime pointers, reusable material or operand digests are published.
